prompt: Many young people leave school with negative attitudes towards learning. What are the causes？How to encourage young people to study？
essay:
In recent years, it was reported that more and more young people have left school with negative attitudes towards learning. This essay will discuss some causes of this phenomenon and propose potential solutions.

The first reason points to the insurmountable workload students receive each day. On top of lengthy school hours, most schools assign pupils piles of homework. As a result, they may feel that their time for hobbies or socialising is being taken away solely to submit their assignments on time, like clockwork. This leads them to feel increasingly unproductive as they gradually lose time to unwind or decompress, both of which are crucial for their mental well-being.Another possible cause can be the teachers' teaching styles. To illustrate, many teachers may adopt rigid, strict teaching approaches, which can make lessons feel repetitive and demotivating, thereby limiting students' passion for learning.

Moreover, some teachers with stern demeanours may be a major contributing factor to pupils' willingness to attend classes, as fear may be instilled in them.There are a few remedies that come to mind for this particular crisis. To begin with, teachers should keep schoolwork within the confines of the classrooms. In other words, students should be allowed to complete their tasks in class so that more time is available to them at home. This procedure can significantly prevent learning fatigue, as they now have more time to engage in recreational activities of their choice. Secondly, teachers can adopt more flexible and interactive teaching strategies, such as role-playing and brainstorming sessions, which more effectively support young scholars in developing their cognitive plasticity and fostering a more engaging educational environment.

To summarise, pessimistic outlooks on learning stem from various causes, from daunting workloads to inflexible teaching methods. However, with appropriate tactics, these issues can be resolved, resulting in a more positive outcome for future students.
